tools.label: ESLint
tools.why: nothing checks the frontend sources, so a wrong import is found by the build or not at all
tools.legacyWhy: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8

tools.label: Stylelint
tools.why: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly

tools.label: Psalm
tools.why: the PHP side has no static analysis, which is what catches a wrong type before the server does

tools.label: PHPUnit
tools.why: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change

tools.label: PHP-CS-Fixer
tools.why: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command

tools.label: REUSE
tools.why: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for

tools.label: EditorConfig
tools.why: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does

lines: composer.json is present but does not parse as JSON.
Every tool that reads it fails the same way, so nothing this file states could be taken into account here.
appinfo/info.xml states no <repository>.

<repository> is the only machine-readable link from a published release back to the source it was built from, and <bugs> is where the App Store page sends a report. Without them a user of the release has no way back to the project.
Declares Nextcloud 29 to 31; the oldest maintained major is 32 (as of 2026-09), the newest released 35 (the release tags of nextcloud/server).
max-version 31 is below the oldest maintained major (32, as of 2026-09), so the release covers only servers that no longer receive fixes.
min-version 29 reaches below the oldest maintained major (32), which means the code has to keep working with APIs that are no longer tested upstream.
engines.node ^20.0.0 in package.json admits only end-of-life Node lines: the release is built on Node 20, which reached end of life on 2026-04-30.
That Node receives no security fixes, and the lockfile is resolved for it. The oldest line still maintained is Node 22.
Node release dates from schedule.json in nodejs/Release, as of 2026-10-23.
package.json without a lockfile.
Every install resolves the ranges afresh, so two builds of the same commit can contain different code, and npm ci - what CI uses - does not run at all.
composer.json without composer.lock.
An app ships its vendor tree, so the versions in it are part of the release; committing the lockfile is what makes that tree reproducible.
package.json script lint calls eslint, and no ESLint configuration is in the checkout.
eslint src
The command is there to be run, so whoever runs it gets a tool that has nothing to go by - and CI, if it runs the script, reports the failure as the change under test.
The app id is pride_flags, the checkout directory is nextcloud-pride-flags.

The server finds an app by its directory name, so the installed directory has to be named after the id. A checkout can be named anything, which is why this is a note and not a defect - but a tarball built from this directory name would not load.
Node stated as ^20.0.0 (package.json engines.node).
Not stated in .nvmrc, so nothing keeps the other places from drifting away from it.
Tooling in the checkout: Stylelint (stylelint.config.js), Psalm (psalm.xml).
No ESLint configuration: nothing checks the frontend sources, so a wrong import is found by the build or not at all.
No PHPUnit configuration: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change.
No PHP-CS-Fixer configuration: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command.
No REUSE configuration: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for.
No EditorConfig configuration: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does.

6 declared packages are named nowhere in the checkout: @nextcloud/vue, @nextcloud/eslint-config, @nextcloud/stylelint-config, @nextcloud/webpack-vue-config, eslint-webpack-plugin, stylelint-webpack-plugin.

Searched as literal names over 30 files, package.json excluded apart from its non-dependency fields, lockfiles excluded; then as an ESLint shorthand, as what TypeScript takes from a tsconfig, and as a peer of an installed package in package-lock.json. A package loaded some other way is not named anywhere either, so this is a list to check, not a list to remove.
Licence gpl3 (appinfo/info.xml), GPL-3.0-or-later (package.json).

gpl3 in appinfo/info.xml is a deprecated App Store value, shown there as GPLv3, which does not say whether -only or -or-later is meant. An SPDX id there needs a <nextcloud> min-version of 31 or higher.
No LICENSES/ directory, so the licence text itself is not in the checkout, which is what REUSE and the distributions check for.
Version 1.1.2 in appinfo/info.xml and package.json.
The ncmake bootstrap stub is in place (21 lines).
Every directory the shipped PHP reaches through __DIR__ and the frontend through linkTo is in the shipped file set (the ncmake core and ncmake.mk).
